items.stem: On December 1, 2026, a hospital asks whether every listed COVID-19 DRUG EUA ended when HHS announced the termination on June 29, 2026. FDA's posted notice gives the effective termination date as June 29, 2027. Which conclusion is correct?

choices.text: The FDA notice sets June 29, 2027 as the effective termination.
choices.why: Correct. The declaration termination was announced in 2026 but applies to listed COVID-drug/biologic EUAs beginning June 29, 2027, absent intervening changes.

choices.text: The listed EUAs ended with the 2026 announcement.
choices.why: Incorrect. The planned termination takes effect in June 2027, not on the announcement date.

choices.text: The listed EUAs continue only after each manufacturer requests a new extension.
choices.why: Incorrect. The FDA notice specifies a termination effective date and does not require a fresh extension to cover the time before it.

choices.text: The notice withdraws the existing FDA-approved indications of these medicines.
choices.why: Incorrect. EUA termination does not automatically rescind independent NDA/BLA approvals.

items.citation: FDA Emergency Use Authorizations for Drugs and Non-Vaccine Biological Products (termination notice); 21 U.S.C. §360bbb-3(b),(g)
items.novelty_rationale: Separates announcement date from later legal effect; does not confuse EUA termination with FDA drug approval.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: An investigational drug is being furnished under an active FDA Emergency Use Authorization with required patient/caregiver information conditions. Which information is part of the federal EUA framework for recipients of an unapproved product? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The EUA establishes the drug's full marketing approval.
choices.why: Incorrect. Emergency authorization is a separate status and is not ordinary marketing approval.

choices.text: Information that the drug is authorized for emergency use and what known and potential risks remain uncertain.
choices.why: Correct. Section 564(e)(1)(A)(ii) calls for informing individuals of emergency authorization, known and potential benefits/risks and uncertainties.

choices.text: The option to accept or refuse administration, potential consequences of refusal, and available alternatives.
choices.why: Correct. 21 U.S.C. §360bbb-3(e)(1)(A)(ii)(III) describes recipients' informed choice and alternatives.

choices.text: A promise that no adverse effects can occur once the patient signs the EUA fact sheet.
choices.why: Incorrect. Emergency authorization necessarily includes potential risks and uncertainties; no such guarantee exists.

items.citation: 21 U.S.C. §360bbb-3(e)(1)(A)(ii)(I)-(III); active authorization-specific healthcare provider/patient fact sheet
items.novelty_rationale: Statutory recipient disclosure and refusal protections rather than another EUA age or treatment-time calculation.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem:
PURCHASE REVIEW
Bottle A: product made and labeled in compliance with a particular U.S. FDA-approved NDA. Bottle B: foreign-labeled version with the same active ingredient and nominal strength, but manufactured outside the terms of the U.S. approval. Both suppliers claim 'same drug.' Which conclusion is supported?

choices.text: The ingredient name alone makes Bottle B an FDA-approved version under Bottle A's NDA.
choices.why: Incorrect. The U.S. approval extends to an approved application and its authorized manufacturing and labeling conditions.

choices.text: Bottle B cannot be presumed FDA-approved simply because its active ingredient and strength match Bottle A.
choices.why: Correct. FDA notes foreign-made versions not manufactured pursuant to a U.S. approval may be unapproved new drugs.

choices.text: All foreign-manufactured drugs are categorically disallowed even when properly made and imported under an FDA-approved application.
choices.why: Incorrect. Foreign manufacture can be lawful when it follows applicable FDA approvals, establishment requirements and import rules.

choices.text: The customer's foreign prescription converts Bottle B to a licensed U.S. generic.
choices.why: Incorrect. A prescription does not create an NDA/ANDA approval or legal importation authorization.

items.citation: 21 U.S.C. §§355(a), 381; FDA import requirements for FDA-approved human drugs
items.novelty_rationale: Exact U.S. approved application/manufacturing pathway versus foreign version with identical ingredient.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: A Massachusetts retail pharmacy proposes importing a foreign-market prescription medicine in bulk to resell to local patients. A customer presents a prescription from an overseas clinician and says the medicine would also qualify for FDA's personal-importation policy if brought for their own use. No FDA-authorized commercial importation pathway has been established. Which conclusions are defensible? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: The foreign prescription substitutes for FDA marketing approval.
choices.why: Incorrect. The legality of marketing/importing a drug is separate from a patient's prescription.

choices.text: A claimed three-month personal supply permits unlimited bulk importation for retail resale.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA's personal-importation considerations do not exempt wholesale commercial stocking.

choices.text: The personal-importation discretion described by FDA does not authorize a pharmacy to stock and resell unapproved foreign-market medicine.
choices.why: Correct. FDA defines personal importation as not for further sale or distribution; enforcement discretion is not a retail import license.

choices.text: The pharmacy needs to assess the product's U.S. approval and lawful distribution/import status separately from the patient's personal-use claim.
choices.why: Correct. Commercial pharmacy importation is not the same as a possible case-by-case FDA enforcement decision for an individual.

items.citation: 21 U.S.C. §§355(a),381; FDA Personal Importation policy (personal use vs resale)
items.novelty_rationale: Separates personal enforcement discretion from commercial retail acquisition instead of testing out-of-state prescription validity.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: A 503A pharmacy compounds from an eligible bulk substance with a valid USP monograph. The bulk supplier's manufacturing establishment is FDA-registered, but the shipment has NO valid certificate of analysis. Assume all other conditions are met. Which federal 503A requirement is still unsatisfied?

choices.text: The compound requires its own FDA-approved NDA.
choices.why: Incorrect. Eligible patient-specific 503A preparations may qualify for statutory exemptions from new drug approval, subject to 503A conditions.

choices.text: The source substance must be in a DEA Schedule II container.
choices.why: Incorrect. Drug scheduling does not supply the missing 503A documentation condition.

choices.text: The substance must come from an overseas manufacturer rather than a registered domestic establishment.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA registration and applicable quality requirements matter, not a blanket foreign-source requirement.

choices.text: The bulk substance must be accompanied by a valid certificate of analysis.
choices.why: Correct. Section 503A bulk-substance conditions require a valid COA in addition to eligibility and manufacturing-establishment registration.

items.citation: FD&C Act §503A(b)(1)(A)(i), 21 U.S.C. §353a(b)(1)(A)(i); FDA 503A bulk drug substances
items.novelty_rationale: Tests missing COA on otherwise eligible bulk supply, not routine patient-specific compounding records or BUD.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem:
COMMERCIAL IMPORT FILE
A U.S. pharmacy chain intends to import a medicine made at an FDA-registered foreign plant in compliance with its U.S.-approved NDA. The importer argues that because both conditions are met, no separate import-entry filing is necessary. What federal import procedure still applies?

choices.text: The pharmacy license substitutes for import entry.
choices.why: Incorrect. State pharmacy licensure does not replace federal customs import-entry procedures.

choices.text: Manufacturer registration eliminates the entry bond and notice.
choices.why: Incorrect. Facility registration and lawful product approval do not remove import entry reporting requirements.

choices.text: Submit an entry notice and bond pending FDA admissibility review.
choices.why: Correct. FDA describes notice of entry and entry bond under customs procedures while FDA reviews admissibility of imported regulated goods.

choices.text: A personal traveler's import policy governs this corporate shipment.
choices.why: Incorrect. This is commercial importation rather than a noncommercial personal import.

items.citation: 21 U.S.C. §381(a); FDA import requirements for FDA-approved human drug products
items.novelty_rationale: Replaced duplicate D014 personal-use-versus-wholesale decision with independently required commercial customs entry notice, entry bond and admissibility review.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: A community pharmacy is revising its hazardous-drug program. Staff find a drug on the 2024 NIOSH hazardous-drug list and are evaluating OSHA and Massachusetts requirements. Which statements correctly describe the source hierarchy? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: A drug's omission from NIOSH removes the employer's OSHA duties.
choices.why: Incorrect. The OSHA standard depends on the chemical hazard and workplace exposure facts, not solely a NIOSH listing.

choices.text: The NIOSH list helps identify a hazardous drug but does not itself confer a DEA controlled-substance Schedule.
choices.why: Correct. The NIOSH list is a worker-exposure identification resource, not the federal Controlled Substances Act scheduling table.

choices.text: OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard imposes its own applicable employer duties for covered workplace hazards.
choices.why: Correct. 29 CFR 1910.1200 can require employer communication, safety information, and employee training.

choices.text: The NIOSH publication alone authorizes pharmacy management to ignore all applicable Board or USP hazardous-compounding rules.
choices.why: Incorrect. Workplace guidance does not override enforceable state practice and compounding requirements.

items.citation: NIOSH List of Hazardous Drugs in Healthcare Settings, 2024; 29 CFR 1910.1200; applicable Massachusetts Board rules
items.novelty_rationale: Distinguishes a federal hazard-reference list from DEA drug scheduling and enforceable OSHA/state workplace practice obligations.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: Under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard, which drug presentation fits its express 'solid, final form for direct administration to the patient' exemption?

choices.text: An intact finished tablet intended to be handed directly to the patient for administration.
choices.why: Correct. 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(6)(vii) excepts a covered drug in solid final form for direct patient administration; other rules may still govern it.

choices.text: An antineoplastic powder transferred into open containers for staff mixing.
choices.why: Incorrect. Open powder handling is not an intact solid finished tablet for direct patient administration.

choices.text: A drug tablet manufactured specifically to be crushed by employees before routine administration.
choices.why: Incorrect. OSHA explains that tablets intended for employee crushing before administration are not in final form under this exemption.

choices.text: A concentrated hazardous-drug solution being diluted by a technician for infusion.
choices.why: Incorrect. A liquid requiring manipulation is outside the stated solid-final-form exemption.

items.citation: 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(6)(vii); OSHA Hospital Pharmacy HCS eTool
items.novelty_rationale: Tests scope of OSHA HCS final-solid-form exemption independent of C103 hazardous crushing/USP containment.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: An FDA-labeled hazardous prescription medicine is subject to the labeling requirements of the FD&C Act. The employer believes this makes all OSHA Hazard Communication requirements disappear. Which narrower conclusion follows from 29 CFR 1910.1200?

choices.text: FDA drug labeling removes the employer's duty to assess exposure and provide applicable worker training.
choices.why: Incorrect. OSHA's FDA-drug-labeling exception is not a blanket exemption from all workplace hazard communication duties.

choices.text: The FDA-label exception is limited; OSHA SDS and worker training may still apply.
choices.why: Correct. 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(5)(iii) addresses HCS labeling; other criteria-based duties still apply.

choices.text: The FDA-label exception applies only after repackaging.
choices.why: Incorrect. The OSHA exception depends on FDA labeling requirements, not the fact of repackaging.

choices.text: The exception removes SDS duties while leaving employee-training duties.
choices.why: Incorrect. FDA-labeling treatment does not itself remove applicable SDS requirements.

items.citation: 29 CFR 1910.1200(b)(5)(iii), (g),(h); OSHA Hospital Pharmacy Hazard Communication Standard eTool
items.novelty_rationale: Tests the precise FDA labeling exception to OSHA labeling only, not dispensing label standards or hazard training.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.

items.stem: A hospital pharmacy adds a new hazardous agent to a work area. Pharmacy technicians and housekeepers may encounter accidental spills during normal duties or foreseeable emergencies. Which OSHA Hazard Communication responses are appropriate? SELECT ALL THAT APPLY.

choices.text: Provide effective hazard information and training for exposed workers when the new hazard is introduced.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1910.1200(h)(1) applies at initial assignment and when a new chemical hazard not previously covered is introduced.

choices.text: Hazard training is reserved for pharmacists signing orders.
choices.why: Incorrect. OSHA's covered exposure provisions include relevant support staff and housekeepers.

choices.text: Wait for an actual spill before making safety information available to housekeeping staff.
choices.why: Incorrect. Foreseeable emergency exposure is part of the standard; proactive training and information are required.

choices.text: Explain accessible SDS, hazard detection, protective measures and emergency procedures to affected workers.
choices.why: Correct. Section 1910.1200(h)(2)-(3) requires effective information and training about hazards and protections.

items.citation: 29 CFR 1910.1200(h)(1)-(3); OSHA hazardous drug exposure guidance
items.novelty_rationale: Tests non-pharmacist hazard-training coverage when a new drug is introduced, not USP HD crushing or drug name recognition.
items.copyright_policy: Original educational scenario; not actual secure MPJE question.
